title: Harness capture computes crisis banner_y from raw constants — under ui_scale > 1 with health on, the blessed frame diverges from the app's scaled layout
detail: Path health_on && ui_scale>1: at ×1.50 the scaled card spans y −5..76 but the banner anchors at unscaled 70 — 6px overlap; the app renders it at hud(70)=105, clear. No current demo combines the directives; the path is unguarded, so a future bless pins app-divergent pixels.
recommended_fix: In capture_frame, mirror the app: banner_y = rnd.hud(&rc.view, 10 + rnd.HEALTH_CARD_H + 6) (and hud the bare 10), keeping ×1.00 byte-identical.

title: Still present since round 1: the parity matrix never runs under any a11y mode — settings chip/row hit rects only ever driven at ×1.00/Off
detail: Every scenario, including the new settings-panel leg, runs with ui_scale=1.0, reduced_motion=false, mode Off. The hud()-scaled rect/hit paths (chip width, row rects — the r1 B2/B5 overlap class) are never driven above ×1.00 anywhere.
recommended_fix: Run the parity matrix once at ui_scale 1.50 (or per a11y mode); at minimum add a scaled settings-chip/row leg so the scaled hit paths execute.

title: Still present since round 1: a11y oracle picks the 40-vs-48 threshold by pr[0] color-value equality, not pair identity
detail: If a future mode-table edit sets a signal token's color equal to a map token's value, that signal pair silently falls under the looser 40 threshold instead of 48 — separation strictness downgrades with no flag.
recommended_fix: Tag each pair with its threshold class when appended (map vs signal), and switch on that tag instead of comparing pr[0] color values.

title: Mode tables never restyle host/router tones — the spec's frozen Always clause and the derivation script's own comment both claim they do
evidence:
spec-7-3-accessibility-core.md:25 (frozen-after-approval): "Every mode restyles ALL of the view: state triad, lanes, ghost, roofs/host/router tones, packet class colors, water/coast/park map tokens, wire ribbons/crisis outline."
data/palette.json modes keys per mode (verified by load): coast, ghost_bad, ghost_ok, house_roofs, lane_best_effort, lane_express, lane_standard, packet_classes, park, pipe_copper, pipe_fiber, pipe_steel, route_glow, route_tie, state_congested, state_critical, state_healthy, water — no host_body/host_roof/router_body/router_dark/router_led in any mode, while the base palette carries them (data/palette.json:16-20).
tools/derive_a11y_palettes.py:204-210:
    # -- roofs/host/router accents: variety is decorative (never the sole
    #    encoder) but must not collapse into mud. Hand-picked MUTED anchors
    #    per mode (L-spread + the residual axis; no saturation blowouts).
    if mode in ("deutan", "protan"):
        remap["house_roofs"] = [(96, 38, 98), (178, 142, 74), (26, 98, 112), (58, 66, 94)]
    else:
        remap["house_roofs"] = [(130, 54, 38), (112, 106, 44), (36, 100, 60), (72, 80, 112)]
detail: The absent-token path (keep canon base) fires for all five host/router tokens under every mode, and Palette_Token's 16 entries include no host/router token — so the restyle path is structurally unreachable, contradicting the Always clause and the script comment. No palcheck leg covers them.
recommended_fix: Either extend Palette_Token + the three mode tables with host/router anchors (plus a palcheck leg), or true up the spec Always clause and the script comment to drop host/router tones.
